title: Switching the order in the determinant det(id + a b) = det(id + b a) for maps between finite projective modules over any ring
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The statement is Sylvester's determinant identity in the form det(id + a b) = det(id + b a) for two R-linear maps a : M -> N and b : N -> M between finite projective modules over an arbitrary ring R (statement lines 36419-36428). The proof is a three-stage reduction that is not a single routine computation: it first localizes at a prime to make the two modules finite free, then specializes to the universal polynomial ring in the matrix entries and passes to its fraction field so that the identity may be checked over a field of characteristic zero, and finally replaces the determinant by the traces of the powers of the matrix through a universal polynomial, leaving only the classical trace identity Trace((AB)^k) = Trace((BA)^k) (proof lines 36431-36454). The characteristic-zero input is what makes the passage from determinants to traces legitimate, since a determinant of size at most N is a polynomial expression in the traces of the powers there. The whole argument is inside the counted span, which refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.
